recipes.title: Golden Chicken Soup with Kneidlach
recipes.description: The soup they call goldene yoich — bird on the bone given three hours and never once allowed to boil.
instructions: Cover the chicken with cold water and bring slowly to the edge of a boil. Skim the grey foam until it stops coming — that decides whether the broth runs clear.
Leave the onions in their skins — the skin is what gives the gold, not the fat.
Add the root vegetables, allspice and the herbs tied in a bundle.
Simmer 3 hours at the lowest heat there is. The soup never boils — boiling clouds it and there is no way back.
Strain, salt at the end, and cool. The fat that sets on top can be lifted off or left.
Cook the kneidlach in a separate pot and add them to the bowl. This is a meat soup — no cream, no butter.

recipes.title: Kneidlach
recipes.description: Matzo balls that swell as they cook — light or leaden, and only two decisions settle which.
instructions: Beat the eggs with oil, salt and pepper. Add the matzo meal and stir — do not knead. Kneading turns them into rubber.
Add the cold sparkling water. The bubbles are what lift them.
Chill the mixture at least an hour, covered. Without that it will not hold its shape.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil, then drop to a gentle simmer.
Wet your hands and roll walnut-sized balls. They will double — do not pack them tight.
Cook covered for 30 minutes without lifting the lid. Made with oil, these are parve and belong in a meat soup too.

recipes.title: Beet Borscht
recipes.description: A ruby sweet-sour beet soup, served hot in winter and cold in summer.
instructions: Peel and coarsely grate the beets — grating gives a stronger colour than dicing.
Fry the onion in the oil 6 minutes, add the beet and stir 3 minutes.
Add water, bay, sugar and half the lemon juice.
Simmer 45 minutes. The acid goes in early — without it the colour fades to brown.
Add the rest of the lemon juice at the end and correct salt, pepper and sugar until the sweet and sour balance.
Serve hot, or chill overnight and serve cold. Parve — it suits a meat meal and a dairy one alike.

recipes.title: Shav — Cold Sorrel Soup
recipes.description: Sour sorrel leaves melted into a green soup, served cold with sour cream and a hard egg.
instructions: Wash the sorrel and strip the thick stems. The leaves will darken as they cook — that is expected, not spoilage.
Fry the onion in butter 5 minutes, add the grated potato and the water.
Cook 12 minutes, add the sorrel and cook 3 minutes only — longer destroys the sourness.
Blend smooth and correct with salt and a little sugar for balance.
Chill completely, at least 4 hours.
Whisk sour cream into each bowl separately and add half a hard-boiled egg. A dairy dish.

recipes.title: Krupnik — Barley Soup
recipes.description: A thick barley and beef soup, plain and consoling, that fed whole families through winter.
instructions: Soak the dried mushrooms in hot water 30 minutes. Keep the soaking liquid — it is half the flavour.
Boil the beef and skim until the broth runs clear.
Add rinsed barley, onion, carrot and parsley root.
Add the mushrooms and their strained soaking liquid.
Simmer 1½ hours until the barley opens and the soup thickens on its own.
Scatter dill and serve. A meat soup — no sour cream, tempting as it is.

recipes.title: Sweet-and-Sour Cabbage Soup
recipes.description: Cabbage, tomato and beef in a broth balanced between vinegar and sugar — the base holishkes came from.
instructions: Sear the beef, add the onion and fry 8 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and fry 2 minutes until it darkens — that cooks out its raw sourness.
Add cabbage, crushed tomatoes and water to cover.
Simmer 1 hour, then add sugar, lemon and raisins.
Simmer another hour and correct — the aim is that neither one wins, not the sour and not the sweet.
Serve with a slice of challah. A meat soup.

recipes.title: Mushroom and Barley Soup
recipes.description: Krupnik without the meat — dried mushrooms supply the depth the beef would have.
instructions: Soak the dried mushrooms in hot water 40 minutes. Strain through cloth and keep the liquid.
Fry the onion in the oil 8 minutes to a deep gold — all the depth is built here, because there is no meat to do it.
Add the fresh mushrooms and fry 10 minutes until their liquid has gone entirely.
Add barley, carrot, the soaked mushrooms and their liquid.
Simmer 50 minutes until the barley is soft and the soup thick.
Scatter dill. Parve — it goes to a meat meal or a dairy one.

recipes.title: Cold Fruit Soup
recipes.description: Prunes, apricots and apples simmered into a thin compote and served cold, as a first course.
instructions: Soak the dried fruit in hot water 20 minutes and drain.
Simmer water, sugar, cinnamon and cloves 10 minutes into a light syrup.
Add the dried fruit and cook 15 minutes.
Add the diced apple and cook 5 minutes only — it has to stay in pieces, not dissolve.
Lift out the cinnamon and cloves and add the lemon juice.
Chill overnight. Served cold in summer as a first course, not as dessert. Parve.

recipes.title: Potato Soup with Schmaltz
recipes.description: A plain country soup whose whole depth comes from rendered poultry fat and deeply fried onion.
instructions: Melt the schmaltz in a heavy pot and fry the onion 15 minutes to a deep brown — not golden, brown.
Add the diced potato and turn it in the fat for 3 minutes.
Add stock, bay and marjoram.
Simmer 30 minutes until the potato crushes under pressure.
Mash about a third against the side of the pot to thicken and leave the rest in pieces.
Scatter dill. Schmaltz is poultry fat, so this soup is meat — it cannot be served with butter or cream.

recipes.title: Meat Borscht with Flanken
recipes.description: The heavy borscht — beet, cabbage and short rib given three hours together until the soup is a meal.
instructions: Boil the flanken and skim carefully for 15 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and cook 1½ hours until the meat begins to give.
Add the grated beet, cabbage and half the lemon juice.
Cook another hour, then add the potatoes for the final 30 minutes.
Correct with sugar and the rest of the lemon until balanced.
Scatter dill. Meat — and unlike the parve borscht, sour cream is out of the question here.

recipes.title: Gefilte Fish
recipes.description: Sweet, delicate fish quenelles poached in vegetable broth and served cold with horseradish.

ingredients.name: fish heads and bones for stock

instructions: Simmer a stock from the fish heads, bones, a whole onion, carrot and a little sugar — 40 minutes, then strain.
Mix the ground fish with grated onion, eggs, matzo meal, sugar, salt and white pepper.
Chill the mixture 30 minutes, then beat it hard for 3 minutes — the beating is what makes it light instead of dense.
Wet your hands and shape oval quenelles.
Lower them gently into the simmering stock, cover and cook 1½ hours at the lowest heat. Do not stir at all.
Cool in the stock overnight; it will set to jelly. Serve cold with a slice of carrot and horseradish. Parve.

recipes.title: Chopped Liver
recipes.description: Broiled chicken liver, caramelised onion and hard egg — chopped with a knife, never ground.
instructions: The liver must be broiled over open flame first — that is a kashrut requirement, not a matter of taste.
Caramelise the onion in schmaltz for 20 minutes over medium-low heat, to a dark and sweet brown.
Add the broiled liver and warm together 5 minutes only.
Cool everything completely — chopping it warm turns the mixture to paste.
Chop by hand with a knife together with the eggs, not in a processor. The grainy texture is the dish.
Fold in the gribenes, correct salt and pepper, and serve on challah. Meat — schmaltz and gribenes are both poultry fat.

recipes.title: Herring in Oil and Onion
recipes.description: Soaked salt fillets in sunflower oil with onion rings and bay — parve, and served with vodka.
instructions: Soak the herring in cold water 6–8 hours, changing the water three times. Any less and it stays too salt to eat.
Dry well and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Layer into a jar: herring, onion rings, bay, allspice, and repeat.
Mix the oil, vinegar and sugar and pour over until fully covered.
Seal and refrigerate at least 48 hours — below that the onion is still sharp and the oil has not gone in.
Serve cold with rye bread. Parve — it suits the end of a meat meal.

recipes.title: Herring in Sour Cream and Apple
recipes.description: The same fish, a wholly different dish — sour cream, tart apple and dill soften the salt.
instructions: Soak the herring 6–8 hours in cold water with three changes, and dry.
Cut into bite-sized pieces and chop the onion as fine as it will go.
Coarsely grate the apple and toss it with the lemon juice at once so it does not brown.
Fold sour cream, apple, onion, dill and pepper into an even mixture.
Fold the herring through gently and refrigerate at least 12 hours.
Serve cold. A dairy dish — unlike the herring in oil, it cannot follow meat.

recipes.title: Eggs and Onions
recipes.description: Three ingredients and no more — hard egg, raw onion and schmaltz or oil. The plainness is the dish.
instructions: Boil the eggs exactly 11 minutes, drop into iced water and peel.
Chop the onion very fine and salt it. Rest 10 minutes, then squeeze out the bitter liquid — that is the difference between this dish and raw onion.
Mash the eggs with a fork to coarse crumbs. Not to a paste.
Combine eggs and onion and add the oil gradually until the mixture is moist and holds together.
Season generously — black pepper is the only spice here.
Serve on challah or matzo. Parve with oil; made with schmaltz it is meat.

recipes.title: Ptcha
recipes.description: Calf's feet simmered four hours with garlic, the broth setting by itself into clear jelly.
instructions: Soak the feet in cold water 2 hours, scrub well and blanch 10 minutes. Discard that water entirely and refill with fresh.
Add onion, bay and allspice and simmer 4 hours at the lowest heat.
Lift out the meat, strip it from the bones and chop fine. Strain the broth through cloth.
Crush the garlic and stir it into the hot broth. The garlic goes in at the end — long cooking makes it bland.
Arrange the chopped meat and sliced egg in a dish and pour the broth over.
Chill overnight until fully set. Cut into squares and serve cold with horseradish. Meat.

recipes.title: Schmaltz and Gribenes
recipes.description: Chicken fat rendered slowly with onion, and the skin left behind turned to crisp gribenes.
instructions: Cut the skin and fat small and put them in a heavy pot with a quarter cup of water.
The water stops it catching in the first minutes, before the fat begins to run. It boils away on its own.
Cook over very low heat for 40 minutes. The fat separates gradually and the skin shrinks.
Add the sliced onion for the last 20 minutes only — onion added early will burn.
When the skin is golden and crisp and the onion brown, strain: the liquid is schmaltz, the solids are gribenes.
Keep the schmaltz refrigerated up to two months. Both are meat — schmaltz is the butter substitute of a meat meal.

recipes.title: Beet Chrein
recipes.description: Grated horseradish root with beet and vinegar — sharp enough to bring tears, and the only thing that belongs beside gefilte.
instructions: Peel the horseradish and cut it into chunks. Open a window and work near it — the fumes are far sharper than onion.
Grind the horseradish in a processor. Keep your face away when you lift the lid.
Add the chopped cooked beet and process to an even deep pink.
Add vinegar, sugar and salt and mix. The vinegar stops the heat developing — any earlier and the chrein stays weak.
Transfer to a sealed jar and refrigerate at least 24 hours.
Keeps two months refrigerated; the heat fades with time. Parve.

recipes.title: Carp in Jelly
recipes.description: Whole fish slices poached in stock and served inside the jelly that sets around them.
instructions: Simmer a strong stock from the heads, bones, onion, parsley root and allspice — 45 minutes. Strain through cloth.
Return the stock to a wide pot and lay the fish steaks in a single layer, not crowded.
Add the sliced carrot and sugar and poach 20–25 minutes at the lowest heat.
Lift the fish out gently with a wide spatula and arrange in a shallow serving dish.
Reduce the stock 10 minutes, correct the salt, and pour it over the fish.
Chill overnight. The gelatine from the bones sets the stock with nothing added. Parve.

recipes.title: Kishke
recipes.description: A filling of flour, vegetables and schmaltz baked in a casing and cut in thick slices — usually inside the cholent.
instructions: Mix flour, semolina, paprika, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Grate the onion, carrot and celery and do not squeeze them — their liquid is all the moisture in the recipe.
Add the melted schmaltz and mix to a thick paste that clings to the spoon.
Turn onto a roasting sleeve or parchment, roll into a thick sausage and seal both ends well.
Bake at 180°C for 1½ hours, or bury it in the cholent and let it cook there overnight.
Cool 20 minutes before slicing. Meat — schmaltz is poultry fat.

recipes.title: Cholent
recipes.description: The pot that sits on a low flame from Friday to Saturday noon — beans, barley, meat and potato melting into one thing.
instructions: Soak the beans overnight and drain. Unsoaked beans will not soften even in twelve hours.
Fry the onion in schmaltz at the base of the pot for 12 minutes to a deep brown, then sear the meat on top of it.
Layer in: beans, barley, whole potatoes, and the eggs in their shells tucked between them.
Scatter paprika, salt and pepper and add boiling water to two centimetres above everything. That is the amount — no more.
Bring to the boil on the hob, then move to a 100°C oven or a hotplate for the night.
Do not open it and do not stir until serving. The eggs come out brown. Serve with kishke and chrein.

recipes.title: Kreplach
recipes.description: Thin dough parcels filled with meat, served in the chicken soup or fried in schmaltz.
instructions: Knead flour, eggs, water and salt into a firm, elastic dough, 8 minutes. Wrap and rest an hour — unrested dough springs back and will not roll.
Chop the cooked beef fine and mix with the fried onion, egg, schmaltz, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough very thin and cut 7 cm squares.
Place a teaspoon of filling in the centre, brush the edges with water and fold into a triangle. Press the air out before sealing — trapped air bursts the parcel as it cooks.
Boil in salted water 12–15 minutes: until they float, then two minutes more.
Serve in chicken soup, or fry in schmaltz until golden. Meat.

recipes.title: Slow-Braised Brisket
recipes.description: A whole brisket in onion and wine, four low hours, and sliced against the grain or ruined.
instructions: Dry the joint well and sear it in a heavy pot to a deep brown on every side — twelve patient minutes.
Lift it out and fry the onion in the same fat for 15 minutes until brown and sweet.
Add the tomato paste and fry 2 minutes, then the wine. Scrape the base until everything browned lifts off.
Return the joint fat side up and add stock, garlic and bay to two-thirds of the meat's height.
Cover and bake at 150°C for 3½–4 hours.
Cool completely before slicing, ideally overnight. Slice against the grain and return to the sauce to reheat. Meat.

recipes.title: Holishkes — Stuffed Cabbage
recipes.description: Cabbage leaves rolled around meat and rice in a sweet-sour tomato braise with raisins.
instructions: Core the cabbage and lower the whole head into boiling water. Peel the leaves off one by one as they soften.
Shave down the thick rib of each leaf with a knife so it rolls without tearing.
Mix beef, uncooked rice, grated onion, salt and pepper — the rice swells inside the braise and drinks the sauce.
Put a spoonful in each leaf, fold the sides in and roll tight.
Pack the rolls seam side down in a pot lined with spare cabbage leaves so they cannot open.
Add tomatoes, sugar, lemon and raisins and cook covered 2 hours over low heat. Meat.

recipes.title: Meat Tzimmes
recipes.description: Carrot, prune and sweet potato cooked with flanken until everything is sweet, orange and glossy — the Rosh Hashanah dish.
instructions: Sear the meat in oil in a heavy pot until browned all over.
Add water to partly cover and cook covered 1½ hours, until the meat begins to give.
Add carrot, sweet potato, prunes, honey, orange juice and cinnamon.
Cook another 1½ hours over low heat, stirring as little as possible — the carrot falls apart easily.
Uncover for the last 20 minutes so the sauce reduces and glazes.
Correct the salt — the sweetness needs it not to become wearying. Meat.

recipes.title: Beef Smothered in Onion
recipes.description: One joint, six onions and almost no liquid — the onion collapses and becomes the sauce itself.
instructions: Sear the joint in hot oil in a heavy pot until deeply browned. Set aside.
Fry all six onions in the same fat over medium heat, 20 minutes, until they reduce to a third and turn brown.
Return the joint to sit in the onion bed and scatter with paprika, salt, pepper and bay.
Add half a cup of water and no more — the onion releases its own. Any more and this becomes a soup.
Cover tightly and cook 3 hours at the lowest heat, turning once halfway.
Rest 20 minutes, slice against the grain and return to the onion sauce. Meat.

recipes.title: Stuffed Chicken Neck
recipes.description: Neck skin sewn into a sleeve and filled with flour and schmaltz — a kitchen that threw nothing away.
instructions: Clean the neck skins well and sew the narrow end shut with kitchen thread.
Mix flour, grated onion, schmaltz, gribenes, paprika, salt and pepper into a thick paste.
Fill each sleeve two-thirds only — the filling swells, and a full sleeve splits as it cooks.
Sew the other end and prick the skin in several places with a needle.
Simmer in chicken soup for an hour, then move to a 200°C oven for 30 minutes until the skin crisps.
Cut into thick slices and serve hot. Meat.

recipes.title: Flanken with Sauerkraut
recipes.description: Short ribs and sauerkraut cooked together until the cabbage's acid takes the meat apart.
instructions: Rinse the sauerkraut in cold water and squeeze. Rinse it partly — the aim is to soften the acid, not remove it.
Sear the flanken in oil until browned all over and lift out.
Fry the onion 8 minutes, add the sauerkraut, caraway and allspice and stir 5 minutes.
Add the grated apple — it balances the acid without adding sugar.
Return the meat, add stock and cook covered 2½ hours over low heat.
Salt only at the end — sauerkraut is salty already. Meat.

recipes.title: Beef Liver with Onions
recipes.description: Thick liver slices, broiled first and then fried fast in schmaltz with a great deal of brown onion.
instructions: Broil the liver over open flame on both sides before anything else — a kashrut requirement that precedes every other step.
Caramelise the onion in schmaltz for 20 minutes to a deep brown, and set aside.
Dry the liver slices and dust them in flour mixed with paprika, shaking off the excess.
Raise the heat high and fry 2–3 minutes a side, no more. Overcooked liver turns grainy and bitter.
Return the onion, season, and toss 30 seconds off the heat.
Serve at once with boiled potatoes. Meat.

recipes.title: Roast Chicken with Schmaltz and Paprika
recipes.description: A whole bird rubbed with schmaltz and paprika on a bed of potatoes that take up everything.
instructions: Mix the schmaltz, paprika, garlic, marjoram and salt into a paste.
Rub the bird outside, inside, and above all under the breast skin — that is where it reaches the meat itself.
Spread onion and potatoes across the tin and set the chicken on them.
Roast covered at 190°C for 60 minutes.
Uncover, baste from the pan juices, and roast another 35–40 minutes until the skin is dark and crisp.
Rest 10 minutes before carving. Meat — the schmaltz makes it so regardless.

recipes.title: Potato Kugel
recipes.description: A kugel with a thick brown crust and a soft middle — all of it decided by oil heated in the tin before the batter goes in.
instructions: Grate the potato and onion alternately — the onion stops the potato darkening while you work.
Squeeze the mixture hard in a cloth. Keep the liquid: the starch settles at the bottom, so pour off the water and return the starch.
Mix with eggs, matzo meal, salt and pepper.
Pour half a cup of oil into the tin and heat it in a 200°C oven until the oil just smokes.
Pour the batter into the hot oil — it should hiss. That is what makes the crust.
Bake 80–90 minutes until dark brown on top. Parve with oil; made with schmaltz it is meat.

recipes.title: Yerushalmi Kugel
recipes.description: Noodles in burnt caramel with coarse black pepper — sweet and sharp at once, and given two and a half hours.
instructions: Boil the noodles until soft, drain and set aside.

Heat the oil and sugar in a heavy pot over medium heat without stirring until the sugar turns dark amber, 8–12 minutes. This step decides everything — too pale and the kugel is bland, too dark and it is bitter.
Pour the boiling caramel over the noodles and stir at once and fast. It will seize for a moment, then melt through.
Cool 20 minutes — hot caramel would cook the eggs.
Fold in the eggs, coarse pepper and salt.
Bake covered at 160°C for 2 hours, then uncover for 30 minutes. Parve.

recipes.title: Sweet Noodle Kugel with Cheese
recipes.description: Wide noodles with cottage cheese, sour cream and raisins — dessert or side, and always dairy.
instructions: Boil the noodles one minute short of the packet — they keep softening in the oven.
Soak the raisins in hot water 10 minutes and drain, so they do not pull moisture out of the kugel.
Mix cottage cheese, sour cream, eggs, sugar and melted butter until smooth.
Fold the noodles and raisins through gently.
Pour into a buttered dish and scatter cinnamon over.
Bake at 180°C for 55–60 minutes until golden and set in the middle. Dairy — it does not follow meat.

recipes.title: Latkes
recipes.description: Deep-fried potato pancakes, lacy at the edges and soft in the middle — the Hanukkah dish.
instructions: Grate the potato and onion together on the coarse side. The onion holds off the browning.
Squeeze hard in a cloth and let the liquid stand 3 minutes — the starch settles. Pour off the water and return the starch to the mixture.
Mix with eggs, matzo meal, salt and pepper, and fry at once. A mixture left standing darkens and weeps.
Heat the oil to 175°C. Too hot and the edges burn while the middle stays raw; too cool and they drink oil.
Drop spoonfuls in and flatten slightly. Fry 3–4 minutes a side to a deep gold.
Drain on a rack, not on paper — paper traps steam and the latke goes soft. Parve.

recipes.title: Applesauce
recipes.description: Tart apples cooked down with cinnamon and lemon to a coarse sauce — the parve companion to latkes.
instructions: Peel and cut the apples into large chunks. Leave a few unpeeled — the skins give a faint pink and more flavour.
Cook with the water, cinnamon stick and lemon zest in a covered pot, 20 minutes.
Uncover, add sugar and lemon juice and cook another 10–15 minutes.
Remove the cinnamon stick and the zest.
Crush with a fork to a coarse texture — a processor turns this into baby food.
Serve warm or cold beside latkes. Parve — which is why latkes can follow meat.

recipes.title: Kasha Varnishkes
recipes.description: Buckwheat and bow-tie pasta with a great deal of fried onion — a side that is nearly a dish.
instructions: Mix the dry buckwheat with a beaten egg until every grain is coated.
Dry it in a hot dry pan for 3 minutes, stirring, until the grains separate. This is what stops it turning to porridge — skip it and the kasha smears.
Add the boiling stock, cover and cook 12 minutes over low heat until absorbed.
Meanwhile fry the onion in the oil for 18 minutes to a deep brown, and boil the pasta.
Combine everything with the onion and the oil left in the pan.
Season generously. Parve with oil; made with schmaltz it is meat.

recipes.title: Parve Carrot Tzimmes
recipes.description: Carrot, prune and honey without meat — the version that can go to a dairy meal.
instructions: Cut the carrots into thick 2 cm rounds — any thinner and they dissolve.
Cook the carrot in the orange juice with a little water for 25 minutes until tender.
Add prunes, honey and cinnamon and cook another 15 minutes.
Mix the flour with 2 tablespoons of cold water and stir it in — it thickens the syrup without cream.
Cook 5 minutes more until the liquid glazes and coats the carrot.
Salt lightly for balance. Parve — unlike the meat tzimmes, it also follows cheese.

recipes.title: Homemade Sauerkraut
recipes.description: Cabbage, salt and time — a natural two-week ferment, with no vinegar and nothing else.
instructions: Weigh the cabbage after coring and take 2% of that weight in salt. That ratio is the whole recipe.
Shred it fine, scatter the salt and massage by hand for 10 minutes until it weeps and softens.
Mix in the caraway, carrot and bay and pack into a jar layer by layer, pressing down hard.
The liquid must cover the cabbage completely. If it does not, top up with a 2% salt brine.
Set a weight on top and cover with cloth. Leave at 18–20°C for 10–14 days.
Skim any foam. When it is sour enough, refrigerate. Parve, and it keeps for months.

recipes.title: Potato Knish
recipes.description: A thin dough wrapper around potato and onion — street food that became a Shabbat pastry.
instructions: Knead flour, oil, water, egg and salt into a soft dough and rest an hour, covered — without the rest it will not stretch thin.
Mash the potatoes while hot and mix with the fried onion, egg, salt and plenty of black pepper.
Roll the dough into a long, very thin strip on a floured cloth.
Lay the filling in a line along one edge and roll into a tight log, using the cloth to help.
Cut into 6 cm pieces, pinch each end closed and press down slightly.
Brush with oil and bake at 190°C for 40–45 minutes until golden. Parve.

recipes.title: Cheese Blintzes
recipes.description: Paper-thin crepes filled with sweet cheese, folded and fried in butter until golden.
instructions: Whisk flour, milk, eggs and salt into a thin batter. Strain it and rest 30 minutes — resting relaxes the gluten and the crepe comes out tender.
Heat a non-stick pan and grease lightly. Pour a thin ladleful and swirl at once.
Cook on ONE side only, about a minute, until the edges lift. Turn out onto a plate, cooked side down.
Mix the cheese, yolk, sugar and lemon zest into a thick filling.
Put a spoonful on the cooked side, fold in the sides and roll into a tight parcel.
Fry in butter 2–3 minutes a side until golden. Serve with sour cream. Dairy.

recipes.title: Braided Challah
recipes.description: A lightly sweet Sabbath loaf on oil and eggs, braided in six and glazed gold before baking.
instructions: Froth the yeast, sugar and warm water for 10 minutes until high and foaming. No foam means dead yeast and the dough will not rise.
Add eggs, oil, flour and salt and knead 10 minutes to a smooth dough that just tacks to a finger.
Rise 1½ hours covered until doubled, then knock back and divide into strands.
Braid from the middle outwards in both directions — that is how the braid comes out even.
Prove again 45 minutes on the tray. Brush with yolk and scatter sesame.
Bake at 180°C for 28–32 minutes. Parve — made with oil and not butter, so it belongs on a meat table.

recipes.title: Hamantaschen
recipes.description: Triangular cookies filled with poppy seed or prune — and the trick is chilling the dough twice.
instructions: Mix oil, sugar, eggs, orange juice and zest. Add flour and baking powder and knead only lightly.
Wrap and chill at least an hour. Warm dough smears and will not cut clean rounds.
Roll to 4 mm and cut 8 cm circles.
Put a teaspoon of filling in the centre — no more. Extra filling forces the triangle open in the oven.
Fold in three corners and pinch the three seams hard. Chill the tray another 20 minutes before baking.
Bake at 180°C for 18–20 minutes until only the edges are golden. Parve.

recipes.title: Cream Cheese Rugelach
recipes.description: The original dough — butter and cream cheese in equal weight, rolled around nuts and cinnamon.
instructions: Work the cold butter, cream cheese, flour and sugar only until the dough just comes together. Overworking destroys the flake.
Divide in four, flatten into discs and chill overnight. That long chill is what separates the layers.
Roll each disc into a thin circle and spread a very thin film of jam.
Scatter the walnuts, brown sugar and cinnamon and cut the circle into 8 wedges.
Roll each wedge from the wide base to the point and curve slightly into a crescent.
Chill another 30 minutes, then bake at 180°C for 22–25 minutes. Dairy — butter and cheese, so never after meat.

recipes.title: Chocolate Babka
recipes.description: A butter-rich yeast dough rolled, split lengthwise and twisted so the chocolate shows on the outside.
instructions: Froth the yeast in warm milk with a tablespoon of sugar for 10 minutes.
Add flour, eggs, sugar and salt and knead 8 minutes. Add the soft butter cube by cube and knead 8 more until smooth and glossy.
Rise 1 hour, then chill 2 hours — cold butter dough cuts clean; warm dough smears.
Roll into a rectangle, spread with melted chocolate and roll into a tight log.
Cut the log lengthwise and twist the two halves with the cut sides up, so the layers show.
Prove 45 minutes, bake at 175°C for 38–42 minutes, and brush with syrup the moment it leaves the oven. Dairy.

recipes.title: Honey Cake
recipes.description: The Rosh Hashanah lekach — honey, coffee and spice, and a cake that is better after two days.
instructions: Warm the honey and coffee together until the honey dissolves, and cool completely. Hot honey will scramble the eggs.
Whisk the eggs, brown sugar and oil until even.
Sift the flour, soda, cinnamon and ginger.
Fold in the dry ingredients and the honey-coffee alternately, stopping the moment there are no lumps.
Bake in a loaf tin at 165°C for 55–60 minutes. Too hot an oven burns the honey before the centre sets.
Wrap it cold and wait two days. The flavour rounds out and the crumb turns moist. Parve.

recipes.title: Apple Strudel
recipes.description: Dough stretched by hand until you can see through it, filled with apple, raisins and walnuts.
instructions: Knead flour, oil, water and salt for 10 minutes until very smooth and elastic. Rest an hour, covered, in an oiled bowl.
Spread a cloth on the table and flour it. Stretch the dough over the backs of your hands from the centre outwards until it is translucent.
Fry the breadcrumbs in oil until golden and scatter them over the dough — they absorb the apple juices and stop a soggy base.
Scatter thinly sliced apple, raisins, walnuts, sugar and cinnamon over one third of the sheet.
Roll up using the cloth, fold the ends in and lift onto a tray.
Brush with oil and bake at 190°C for 40–45 minutes. Parve — oil, not butter.

recipes.title: Mandelbrot
recipes.description: Twice-baked almond cookies — hard, dry, and meant to be dipped in tea.
instructions: Whisk eggs, sugar, oil and vanilla. Add flour and baking powder and mix to a soft, sticky dough.
Fold in whole almonds, not chopped. They are what gives the bite.
Shape two flat logs on a tray, about 8 cm wide. They will spread.
Bake at 175°C for 30 minutes until set but still pale.
Take them out and slice while hot with a serrated knife into 1.5 cm pieces, then lay them flat.
Scatter sugar and cinnamon and return for 20–25 minutes until dry. Parve, and keeps for weeks.

recipes.title: Kichel
recipes.description: Airy, light cookies from four ingredients that puff up like pillows in the oven.
instructions: Beat the eggs for 5 minutes until pale and foaming — that is all the lift there is, since there is no raising agent.
Add the oil in a thin stream while still beating.
Fold in the flour, sugar and salt gently, mixing no more than needed.
Scatter sugar generously on a surface, drop spoonfuls of dough and roll them in it on both sides.
Flatten into thin rounds and space them widely — they double in area.
Bake at 175°C for 28–30 minutes until golden and puffed. Parve.

recipes.title: Teiglach
recipes.description: Tiny dough balls cooked in boiling honey syrup until they swell and turn gold.
instructions: Knead flour, eggs, oil and salt into a firm dough. Roll into thin ropes and cut into chickpea-sized pieces.
Heat honey, sugar and ginger in a wide pot to a steady gentle boil.
Add all the dough balls at once and cover immediately. Shake the pot; never stir with a spoon.
Cook covered 20 minutes without lifting the lid — they swell on the trapped steam.
Uncover, shake again, and cook 20–25 minutes until golden brown and hollow-sounding.
Add a quarter cup of boiling water carefully — the syrup will foam. Stir in the nuts and turn out onto oiled paper. Parve.

recipes.title: Dried Fruit Compote
recipes.description: Prunes, apricots and figs in a light cinnamon syrup — the dessert that was always in the fridge.
instructions: Rinse all the dried fruit in cold water.
Simmer water, sugar, cinnamon and lemon slices 8 minutes into a light syrup.
Add the prunes, apricots and figs and cook 20 minutes over low heat.
Add the raisins for the last 5 minutes only — any earlier and they fall apart entirely.
Lift out the cinnamon stick and the lemon slices.
Chill overnight. The flavour deepens in the cold, not in the cooking. Served cold. Parve.
